JWST (MIRI) made the first secure detection of the neutral methyl radical CH3 around a dying carbon-rich star, SMP LMC 011 in the Large Magellanic Cloud (published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, 2026). CH3 is symmetric and radio-silent, and its identifying vibration is in the mid-infrared blocked by Earth's atmosphere, so it could only be caught by a space telescope. The measured abundance (~5.6e17 cm-2) is far larger than standard UV-breakdown chemistry predicts, supporting a new mechanism: UV photons and shocks erode hydrogenated amorphous carbon dust grains, releasing CH3 directly - making CH3 a key reactive intermediate in building complex hydrocarbons and PAHs in dying stars.

learnings.text: Frontier AI market has fragmented from a single leaderboard into distinct trade-offs (intelligence, cost, speed, coding-agent performance, cyber): model variants (max/high/xhigh) and agent harnesses materially change results - e.g., Claude Code + Sonnet 5.5 tops coding-agent scores at ~$14/task while Codex + GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 92% of that at ~$1/task. Choosing the harness+variant matters more than picking 'the best model'.

Frontier model API pricing pattern: introductory rates set low to match the leader (Gemini 4 Argon $2/$10 per M tokens matches OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol), then published rates double. Price-matching at launch followed by normalization is the standard playbook.

Decision-model layer is commoditizing by subsidy: TypeSafe's Jev (startup, $0.042/M tokens) spawned three near-identical releases in ~17 days - OpenAI's Luna Decisions API, Cloudflare's open Clef/Clef-flash, Amazon's open Strands Decider 2B - with the two infra giants giving it away free and open-weight. Pattern: a thin agent-infrastructure layer gets commoditized by hyperscaler subsidy within weeks of a startup proving demand.

The AI market's battleground has moved from frontier models to personal agents: Meta's Muse app topped the App Store with 5M+ downloads (Sensor Tower, Sep 30) and OpenAI launched its Dots personal agent the same week Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon. JPMorgan noted Google needs a personal-agent breakthrough to convert product velocity into consumer sentiment. Consumer AI adoption is won by free agent apps, not model launches.

AI frontier is shifting toward long-horizon agentic work and on-device inference: Google's Gemini 4 Argon ships a 1M-token output limit (vs 64k before), initially restricted to trusted cyber defenders; AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 400 targets local LLM workloads on workstations for latency/data-residency wins.

Reddit is shutting down RSS (Nov 13) and ending general public API access by March 2027, citing automated AI scraping; developers of bots/approved apps must register by Jan 12, 2027. Pattern: major platforms are closing free/open data access as human-generated content becomes AI training gold (Reddit data licensing up 24% YoY).

Google's developer-verification system adds a 24-hour delay + multi-step friction (developer mode, restart, biometric confirm) for installing apps from unverified developers on certified Android hardware; enforcement began Sep 30, 2026 in Brazil/Indonesia/Singapore/Thailand with global rollout in 2027+. ADB installs are exempt; >99% of Play Store apps are auto-registered, and Google's analysis found 90x more malware in sideload sources than on Play.

End-screen CTR benchmark is about 5 clicks per 1,000 views; below that almost always means the last 30 seconds were not scripted as a deliberate handoff to a named next video. Pairing related videos with end screens pointing specifically at each other compounds Browse and Suggested distribution.

Shorts-to-long-form conversion is a routing problem, not a content problem: target 0.5-1% conversion vs the 0.04% most channels run at. Configure the Related Video link on every Short (Video Details -> Related Video -> parent long-form) - it is the only routing mechanism Shorts support; structure the Short as an incomplete answer with the CTA in the final 3 seconds. One managed channel gained +41.8% views and +64.1% revenue in 30 days from routing fixes alone.

YouTube CTR and retention benchmarks 2026: CTR below 2% is effectively dead, 4-8% gets tested further, 10%+ gets heavy promotion; average view duration below 30% is penalized, 40-60% is good, 60%+ excellent. High CTR paired with low retention is the fastest way to lose reach (reads as a misleading thumbnail).

Gaming channels on YouTube grow best long-form-only: AIR's 2026 analysis of 18,000 channels found gaming channels that skip Shorts have 85% more subscribers than mixed-format ones (the widest gap of any niche). Safe Shorts ratio is 25-40% of uploads; above 55% long-form performance thins; do not shift the ratio more than 30 points in one quarter.

Paywall A/B test priorities: localization wins most (62.3% LTV win rate), then trial structure (59.6%) and plan duration (58.7%); visual/copy tweaks only win 34.6%. Also Google Play involuntary billing failures cause ~31% of cancellations (vs 14% on App Store), so dunning/payment-retry recovery matters on Android.

Offering more plans raises conversion: 1 to 2 plans = +61%, 2 to 3 plans = +44% (Superwall, 32M paywall opens); longest trials convert best (17-32 day trials 42.5% vs <=4 day 25.5%), and trial buyers retain 1.4-1.7x better than direct buyers. For games specifically, keep the free tier: gaming RPI is $0.08 (lowest category), ~77% of mobile game revenue is IAP from free players, and free users are ad inventory not cost.

Hard paywalls convert ~5x better than freemium (10.7% vs 2.1% download-to-paid at Day 35, RevenueCat 2026) and lift LTV ~21% per subscriber, but ~80-90% of trial starts and ~half of paid conversions happen on Day 0 - the paywall must be seen on the first session, not buried deep.

recent_learnings: Frontier AI market has fragmented from a single leaderboard into distinct trade-offs (intelligence, cost, speed, coding-agent performance, cyber): model variants (max/high/xhigh) and agent harnesses materially change results - e.g., Claude Code + Sonnet 5.5 tops coding-agent scores at ~$14/task while Codex + GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 92% of that at ~$1/task. Choosing the harness+variant matters more than picking 'the best model'.

Frontier model API pricing pattern: introductory rates set low to match the leader (Gemini 4 Argon $2/$10 per M tokens matches OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol), then published rates double. Price-matching at launch followed by normalization is the standard playbook.

Decision-model layer is commoditizing by subsidy: TypeSafe's Jev (startup, $0.042/M tokens) spawned three near-identical releases in ~17 days - OpenAI's Luna Decisions API, Cloudflare's open Clef/Clef-flash, Amazon's open Strands Decider 2B - with the two infra giants giving it away free and open-weight. Pattern: a thin agent-infrastructure layer gets commoditized by hyperscaler subsidy within weeks of a startup proving demand.

The AI market's battleground has moved from frontier models to personal agents: Meta's Muse app topped the App Store with 5M+ downloads (Sensor Tower, Sep 30) and OpenAI launched its Dots personal agent the same week Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon. JPMorgan noted Google needs a personal-agent breakthrough to convert product velocity into consumer sentiment. Consumer AI adoption is won by free agent apps, not model launches.

AI frontier is shifting toward long-horizon agentic work and on-device inference: Google's Gemini 4 Argon ships a 1M-token output limit (vs 64k before), initially restricted to trusted cyber defenders; AMD's Ryzen AI Max+ Pro 400 targets local LLM workloads on workstations for latency/data-residency wins.

Reddit is shutting down RSS (Nov 13) and ending general public API access by March 2027, citing automated AI scraping; developers of bots/approved apps must register by Jan 12, 2027. Pattern: major platforms are closing free/open data access as human-generated content becomes AI training gold (Reddit data licensing up 24% YoY).
